title: Communication-Aware Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Robust Satellite Custody Under Range-Limited Links and Sensor Clutter
content: Persistent custody of moving ground targets is comparatively easy when every satellite has clean sensors and global team state. It is not easy under range-limited inter-satellite links (ISL), packet dropout, and slot-level false-positive clutter. In a Keplerian+J2 environment with an honest pointing rule (a tip holds only if the reported contact is on the true target), a memoryless local greedy policy achieves 42.4% mean custody on the HARD preset, and shared-policy PPO saturates near 49%— close to the local true-detection ceiling, not a failed optimizer. A graph-conditioned controller that fuses agreeing neighbor contacts and coasts the last confirmed track recovers 92.2% (heuristic) / 92.4% (hierarchical PPO), matching the privileged geometry reference (91.3%). On the EASY preset (no clutter, global links) local greedy already reaches 93.1%, so the performance gap is a HARDonly phenomenon driven by information and track persistence rather than by the inability of PPO to optimize. The contribution is a cluttered, communication-constrained custody benchmark, anempirical demonstration that local policies collapse to the true-detection ceiling, and a graph-conditioned hierarchical policy (heuristic and learned) that recovers the visibility ceiling.
